newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FACE CRUCIAL MATCH AGAINST UPSTARTS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA FACE CRUCIAL MATCH AGAINST UPSTARTS.

text.p: Argentina, their World Cup fate lying in the balance, face a team on Wednesday who traditionally have not troubled them but who now represent a major threat.
Only a few years ago, Argentina would have scoffed at any suggestion they could lose to Ecuador, their opponents in a crucial qualifier.
The contrasts between their respective soccer traditions could not be stronger.
Argentina are a major soccer power who have won the World Cup twice and hosted it once.

Ecuador are one of two South American countries never to have reached the finals, did not play their first full international until 1938 and, after winning their two inaugural matches, embarked on a run of 22 successive defeats.
The first two meetings of the countries ended in 6-1 and 12-0 wins for Argentina. But things have changed a bit since then with Ecuador now threatening to turn history upside down.

Ecuador lie fourth in the South American World Cup qualifying group, edging Argentina out of the qualifying places on the number of goals scored. The top four in the nine-team group will go to France.
Bolivia, Ecuador, Argentina and Uruguay all have 13 points from nine games.

Argentina were beaten 2-0 when they visited Quito for the teams' first meeting in the competition last year and also lost 1-0 in a friendly before the 1994 World Cup. They have not beaten Ecuador since 1987.

To add further intrigue, Ecuador are coached by the man who masterminded one of the most humiliating days in Argentine soccer history -- Colombia's 5-0 win in Buenos Aires in a World Cup qualifier four years ago.
Former Colombia coach Francisco Maturana, who revolutionised football in his own country in seven years as national team coach, is now trying to do the same for Colombia's smaller neighbour.
The Argentines regard him as a bogeyman.
"I haven't lost to them since 1987, neither there, nor at altitude, nor in the cold, nor in the heat. They must be waiting for me with open arms," he said.
"I have just been lucky and things have worked out. If I were capable of beating Argentina every time, I would be rich."
Argentina's campaign in the group, which has been inconsistent at best, hit a new low last month when they lost 2-1 to Bolivia in La Paz.
Worse still, they had two players sent off and were involved in a brawl at the end which delayed play for ten minutes.
